key_insight: Projecting task gradients into orthogonal subspaces inside a shared LoRA adapter disentangles conflicting updates, eliminating negative transfer and restoring per-task performance close to single-task fine-tuning while keeping parameter efficiency.
problem_solved: Negative transfer in multi-task LoRA: conflicting gradient updates from different tasks degrade individual task performance when a single low-rank adapter is shared across tasks.
method: Detect task-specific gradient components in the shared LoRA adapter and identify conflict directions between tasks.
Apply orthogonal gradient projection to remove or reorient conflicting components so each task updates only non-conflicting subspaces of the adapter.
Maintain LoRA's low-rank structure and lightweight footprint so multi-task adaptation remains parameter- and storage-efficient.
impact: Allows practitioners to deploy one compact LoRA adapter for many tasks without sacrificing per-task accuracy, reducing storage and maintenance costs for multi-task LLM deployments while avoiding negative transfer.
visual_elements: 2D vector diagram: two task gradients shown with the conflicting component projected orthogonally onto a preserved subspace
Architecture sketch: shared LoRA adapter plugged into an LLM with per-task orthogonal projection modules
Bar chart: per-task accuracy comparing single-task fine-tuning, naive multi-task LoRA, and the proposed orthogonal projection method
Table or icon set: storage overhead (number of adapters) vs average task performance to highlight efficiency gains
paper_title: Disentangling Task Conflicts in Multi-Task LoRA via Orthogonal Gradient Projection
paper_authors: Ziyu Yang, Guibin Chen, Yuxin Yang, Aoxiong Zeng, Xiangquan Yang
